channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Ucell Showcases Digital Solutions, Including 5G and Telecom Infrastructure for Wind Farm
item.description: At ICT Week Uzbekistan, Ucell presented digital solutions like 5G, network upgrades, and telecom infrastructure for the Kungrad Wind Power Plant. The company was recognized for its mobile network speed and quality. Ucell also highlighted IoT, AI scoring, and environmental monitoring for businesses.

item.title: Iran's President's Representative States 'Iran Will Not Bow to US' at UN
item.description: Iran's representative Pezeshkiyon stated at the UN that the Islamic Republic is a victim of terrorism and will not bow to the United States. The US delegation reportedly walked out of the hall during his speech.

item.title: Full Leather and Footwear Production Cycle Established in Altinkul, Uzbekistan
item.description: A complete production cycle for the leather and footwear industry is being established in the Altinkul district of Uzbekistan's Andijan region. The industrial zone integrates entrepreneurs and clusters, focusing on raw material processing to finished goods, with 17 projects underway.

item.title: Bishkek Residents Learn About Eco-Friendly Heating Systems
item.description: An informational meeting in Bishkek introduced residents to eco-friendly and energy-efficient heating systems. Attendees learned about state preferential loan conditions for installing heat pumps. The project, supported by the World Bank, offers loans up to 1 million Kyrgyz som at 6% annually.

item.title: US, Denmark, and Greenland Sign Defense Agreement to Expand US Military Presence
item.description: The US, Denmark, and Greenland have signed a security agreement allowing the US to expand its military presence on the island. The deal amends a 1951 defense treaty and could permit the US to establish two additional military bases in Greenland.

item.title: Smart Water Meters for Accurate Consumption Control Produced in Khodjaabad
item.description: Production of smart water meters for precise consumption control has been established in Khodjaabad. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited a technopark and reviewed the manufacturing process. The project, a collaboration with Chinese company Sanchuan and utilizing Huawei technology, aims to improve water management in the densely populated Andijan region.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Kochkor District Still Addressing Aftermath of July Mudflows
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Emergency Situations visited Kochkor district in Naryn region to assess the consequences of July mudflows. Four out of five affected state railway sections are cleared, with plans for protective measures on the remaining one and a new mudflow channel.

item.title: Journalist's Trial in Bishkek Postponed Due to Absent Experts
item.description: A Bishkek court postponed the retrial of journalist Makhabat Tajibek kyzy because key experts failed to appear. Defense questioned an expert's competence, while the prosecution cited language day events and illness. The case relates to media projects Temirov LIVE and Ait, Ait.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ranks First in CIS for Wired Internet Speed
item.description: Uzbekistan has achieved the top position in the CIS for wired internet speed, attributed to years of network modernization efforts. This involved collaboration among communication operators, internet providers, and the main infrastructure provider, Uztelecom.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Visits Artificial Intelligence Center in Baliqchi
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the Artificial Intelligence center in Baliqchi. The head of state familiarized himself with startups created by young people, highly praising their knowledge and intellectual potential. He engaged with the young innovators.

item.title: Navoiyuran State Enterprise Holds Open Meeting with Media on Compliance and Geology
item.description: The Navoiyuran State Enterprise in Uzbekistan held an open meeting with media representatives to discuss its work, results, and tasks. Key topics included anti-corruption measures, compliance systems, geological exploration, and occupational safety, fostering transparency and dialogue.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Cultural Heritage Agency Criticized Over Protection Priorities
item.description: Party chairman Alisher Qodirov criticized Uzbekistan's Cultural Heritage Agency for prioritizing Soviet-era structures over historical monuments. He highlighted an 11th-century building near a ziyarat site, whose preservation is stalled due to funding and new burials. The agency previously stated cultural heritage has no nationality.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enacts Law Mandating Closed Hearings for Juvenile Criminal Cases
item.description: A new Uzbek law, effective September 12, 2026, mandates that criminal cases involving minors will only be heard in closed sessions. This amendment to the Criminal Procedure Code aims to protect minors' privacy, aligning national legislation with international standards on child protection and preventing negative impacts from public trials.

item.title: Uzbekistan launches 206 investment projects in Andijan region
item.description: In Andijan region, Uzbekistan, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev oversaw the launch and commencement of 206 new investment projects. These projects, valued at $9.4 billion, span various sectors including energy, construction, and tourism, aiming to boost industrial development and employment.

item.title: Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, and Turkey commence joint military exercises 'Unity Strength 2026'
item.description: Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, and Turkey have begun joint military exercises named 'Unity Strength 2026' in Azerbaijan. The drills aim to enhance interoperability, experience exchange, and coordinated actions among military personnel using various military equipment, aviation, and drones.

item.title: Tajikistan Mandates HIV Testing for Beauty Salon Staff and Newlyweds
item.description: Tajikistan has implemented a new government decree requiring mandatory HIV testing for beauty salon employees and newlyweds. Those diagnosed with the virus will be prohibited from working in the beauty industry. This requirement was not present in previous regulations and aims to control the spread of infections.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey to Expand Cooperation in Legal Information Sphere
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkey plan to enhance collaboration in legal information exchange, focusing on digitalization of legislative databases and adoption of modern technologies. A recent visit by a Turkish delegation to Uzbekistan's 'Adolat' center facilitated discussions on sharing experiences and developing joint digital solutions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Seizes Over 1.4 Tons of Drugs in Eight Months
item.description: In Uzbekistan, over 12,000 drug-related crimes were detected in the first eight months of the year. During this period, 89 major drug trafficking groups were dismantled. Authorities confiscated 1.4 tons of traditional drugs and 61.7 kg of synthetic substances.

item.title: Russian Tour Operators Report Increased Demand for Uzbekistan Travel
item.description: Russian tour operators have noted a significant rise in demand for tours to Uzbekistan this autumn, with sales up to 65% compared to last year. Classic excursion routes and short city tours are most popular. Increased flight connections are cited as a contributing factor.

item.title: Uzbekistan to produce modern equipment for small hydropower plants in Andijan
item.description: A new enterprise, 'Andijan Jinlun New Energy', will produce modern equipment for small hydropower plants in Andijan, Uzbekistan. The project, valued at $20 million, aims to meet regional demand for specialized equipment and utilize the area's water resources for green energy.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov completes eight-day trip across three continents
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov returned to Bishkek after an eight-day working trip to South Korea and the USA. The journey included visits to Seoul, Utah, and New York, where he addressed the UN General Assembly and met with business representatives.

item.title: Uzbekistan plans 1 GW data center complex in Karakalpakstan powered by renewables
item.description: Uzbekistan will develop a 1 GW data center complex in Nukus district, Karakalpakstan, utilizing renewable energy sources. The project includes building new substations and transmission lines to connect with wind farms, with full capacity expected by late 2028.

item.title: Andijan establishes $28 million leather and footwear industrial zone with 17 projects
item.description: A new leather and footwear industrial zone worth $28 million has been established in Andijan, Uzbekistan. The zone will host 17 projects and has already created 2,500 new jobs.

item.title: Tashkent hosts international conference on modern engineering education approaches
item.description: An international conference on modern engineering education was held at the Tashkent Institute of Textile and Light Industry. The event focused on preparing qualified personnel for modern mechanical engineering and digitalization.

item.title: Andijan textile factory integrates AI and dual education for eco-friendly production
item.description: An Andijan textile enterprise, "Eco Cotton," is implementing artificial intelligence and dual education systems. The project, supported by President Mirziyoyev, focuses on producing eco-friendly textiles from local raw materials for domestic and international markets. The factory invested $10 million, creating 1,000 jobs and aiming for 25 billion soms in annual state budget revenue.

item.title: Andijan launches $25 million 'smart' water meter factory with 80% automation
item.description: A new factory producing "smart" water meters worth $25 million has been launched in Andijan. The production process is 80% automated, with plans to reach 70% localization by 2030. The facility aims to meet future demands for advanced water management technology.

item.title: Bishkek police seize over 6,000 doses of synthetic drugs
item.description: Bishkek police have arrested two individuals suspected of distributing synthetic drugs via hidden caches. Authorities seized approximately 1 kilogram of Alpha-PVP, valued at over 4 million soms, which could constitute more than 6,000 doses. Investigations are ongoing to identify other potential accomplices.

item.title: Russian education remains in demand in Central Asia, says Rossotrudnichestvo representative
item.description: Russian education is highly sought after in Central Asia due to historical and cultural ties, according to Irina Staroselskaya, head of Rossotrudnichestvo in Uzbekistan. Uzbekistan has requested 810 state-funded places for the 2026/27 academic year, with universities noting the diligence of Uzbek students.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Incentives for Businesses Creating Jobs for Low-Income Citizens
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev suggested attracting entrepreneurs to employ low-income citizens by offering preferential loan and tax terms for businesses creating jobs. He emphasized the need for targeted aid, ensuring support reaches those genuinely in need. Local authorities have been granted necessary powers to work with low-income families and ensure employment.

item.title: Tajikistan and China to Expand Cooperation in Training Civil Servants
item.description: Tajikistan's Academy of Public Administration and China's Lanzhou University of Technology signed a Memorandum of Understanding to enhance cooperation in education, research, and academic exchange. The agreement includes plans for faculty and student exchanges, joint research on Central Asian issues, and training programs for Tajik civil servants.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes direct Bishkek-Sanya flight and discusses railway construction with China
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has proposed a direct air service between Bishkek and Sanya to China. Discussions also covered the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, road construction, and border infrastructure. Cooperation in industry, finance, energy, and digital economy was also explored.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan parliament approves self-ban on real estate transactions to combat fraud
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's parliament has approved a bill allowing citizens to impose a self-ban on real estate transactions for up to 72 hours. This measure aims to prevent fraud, particularly for elderly citizens, by providing a cooling-off period before property sales.

item.title: Second International Textile Forum Opens in Dushanbe
item.description: The Second International Textile Forum "Tajikistan-2026" opened in Dushanbe on September 23, 2026. Organized by the Ministry of Industry and New Technologies, the event brought together representatives from 15 countries to discuss the textile industry's development, foreign investment, and international experience exchange.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Direct Bishkek-Sanya Flight Route to China
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has proposed to China the opening of a direct flight route between Bishkek and the resort city of Sanya. Discussions also covered a China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway and infrastructure projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan to resume hosting international ATP and WTA tennis tournaments
item.description: Uzbekistan will resume hosting international tennis tournaments under the auspices of ATP, WTA, and ITF starting October 1, 2026. A presidential decree aims to popularize tennis, develop talented athletes, improve sports infrastructure, and enhance performance in prestigious competitions. Tournament costs will be covered by sponsorships.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and China discuss oil refinery and pipeline construction
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Erlist Akunbekov, met with executives from Chinese oil and gas corporations CNPC and Sinopec in Beijing. The discussions focused on the potential construction of an oil refinery and a related pipeline.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Academy of Law Enforcement granted CIS base status for anti-corruption
item.description: The Academy of Law Enforcement of Uzbekistan has been granted status as a base educational organization of the CIS for combating corruption. This decision was made at the 11th meeting of the Interstate Council for Combating Corruption in Minsk, where member states' representatives participated.

item.title: New School Building Inaugurated in Kurush Village, Spitamen District
item.description: A new school building was commissioned in Kurush village, Spitamen district, on September 22, 2026. The facility, funded by parents, sponsors, and local authorities, accommodates 320 students and features modern classrooms.

item.title: Tajikistan and Belarus Free Economic Zones Discuss Expanding Trade and Investment
item.description: Leaders of Tajikistan's Dangara SEZ and Belarus's Gomel-Raton SEZ held an online meeting to discuss expanding trade and investment cooperation, developing logistics, and exchanging experience. Both sides emphasized strengthening bilateral economic ties and creating favorable investment conditions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Transforms Aral Sea Region Towards Sustainable Development and New Economy
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively transforming the Aral Sea region, moving beyond ecological disaster recovery to foster a new economy. Initiatives include large-scale afforestation, green energy, modern agriculture, and digital technologies, aiming for sustainable development linked to population income and environmental policy.
